audits.title: Improving Carer Experience and Engagement in a Community Rehabilitation Team: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists standards for community rehabilitation services
audits.setting: Specialist community rehabilitation team, Sheffield Health Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Only 3/50 (6%) service users had formally recorded carers; survey response 24% (14/58); 93% had emergency contact information, 78% felt supported, 64% felt involved, 50% aware of carers groups, 14% given written information.

audits.intervention: Bimonthly family, friends and carers support group set up, written carers pack reviewed and definition of carer broadened
audits.other_findings: All 14 respondents identified as carers, suggesting significant under-recording; EPR limits formal recording of carer status.
audits.citation: MacDonnell J. Improving Carer Experience and Engagement in a Community Rehabilitation Team: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S172-S173. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11425.

audits.title: Carer Involvement in Liaison Emergency Assessments at Devon Partnership Trust: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: PLAN standards, NICE suicide and safety planning guidance and Triangle of Care; target 90% carer contact and information-sharing form completion
audits.setting: Three liaison psychiatry teams (Torbay, Exeter, North Devon), Devon Partnership Trust, emergency departments

cycle1.result: Carers not routinely contacted and information-sharing form infrequently completed.

audits.intervention: QI team including a carer representative; staff survey, driver diagram and change ideas focused on workplace culture, with monthly rolling audit of 5 patients per team.

cycle2.result: SPC data initially within normal variability, particularly for documentation; recent positive trend without figures.

audits.citation: Scurr T, Somerville K, Anderson M, Giri N, Manders T. Carer Involvement in Liaison Emergency Assessments at Devon Partnership Trust: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S198-S198. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11478.

audits.title: Triangle of Care in a Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Service: A CaseNote Audit From Telford & Wrekin
audits.standard: Triangle of Care national framework (Carers Trust), six standards; Trust policy and Health and Care Act 2022 duty to involve carers
audits.setting: Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment (CRHT) service, Telford and Wrekin (MPFT)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance across ToC standards 77%. S1 identification 55%, S2 staff training 100%, S3 confidentiality/information sharing 50%, S4 defined carer roles 67%, S5 carer introduction and information 90%, S6 range of carer support 100%.

audits.other_findings: Key gaps: recording special circumstances 27%, documented consent/limits 54%, revisiting non-disclosure 33%, offering support when disclosure declined 0%, carer involvement in discharge planning 50%. Action plan in development with re-audit scheduled for 2026.
audits.citation: Patel S, Bolaji A, Aldakatti C, Turnbull A, Mutasa T. Triangle of Care in a Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Service: A CaseNote Audit From Telford & Wrekin. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S336-S337. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11823.

audits.title: Evaluation of Carer Contact Practices for Junction 17 CAMHS Inpatient Unit

cycle1.result: Assigned staff member 58% (7/12); consent documented 8% (1/12); contact within 72 hours 100%; after medication changes 66% (2/3); after incidents 73% (132/180); after home leave 87%; after ward round 47% (51/108).

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: key family link staff, standardised PARIS documentation, protected time for carer contact and induction training; re-audit in three months.
audits.citation: Shahib A, Cooper A, Dugard R. Evaluation of Carer Contact Practices for Junction 17 CAMHS Inpatient Unit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(Suppl 1):S166-S166.

audits.title: Improving Carers’ Engagement in Patient Care During Psychiatric Admissions
audits.standard: Five key carer engagement domains agreed with patient groups and carer representatives (carer notified of admission, carer care plan, collateral history from carer, carer notified of discharge)
audits.setting: Keats Ward, Meadowbrook Unit, adult female acute psychiatric inpatient unit, Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Carer notified of admission 30%; documented carer care plan 50%; collateral information from carer 30%; carer notified of discharge 40%

audits.intervention: Standardised Carer Contact Form introduced over several PDSA cycles, with staff training and competency assessments for nursing assistants

cycle2.period: November 2024 to July 2025 (re-audit after nine months)
cycle2.result: Carer notified of admission 87%; documented carer care plan 60%; collateral information 87%; carer notified of discharge 80%

audits.other_findings: Staff reported greater confidence engaging with carers and there were fewer complaints from families. Other wards in the unit adopted the form.
audits.citation: Anyim N, Grindey A, Asher C. Improving Carers’ Engagement in Patient Care During Psychiatric Admissions. BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S136-S137.
